root_cause.text: The `rtw_core_enable_beacon()` function in the rtw88 driver performs 32-bit register operations on the `REG_TXPAUSE` register, which is located at an unaligned address (0x522), triggering an alignment fault on architectures that require aligned MMIO accesses.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `rtw_write32_clr` and `rtw_write32_set` with `rtw_write8_clr` and `rtw_write8_set` for `REG_TXPAUSE`. Additionally, the crash log shows an alignment fault (`FSC = 0x21: alignment fault`) at virtual address `ffff8000827e0522` (offset `0x522`) originating from `rtw_pci_read32` called via `rtw_core_enable_beacon`.

Author: Po-Hao Huang <phhuang@realtek.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 16 20:55:38 2023 +0800

    wifi: rtw88: Stop high queue during scan
    
    When traversing channel list, TX in high queue should be disabled

    Signed-off-by: Po-Hao Huang <phhuang@realtek.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability by adding 32-bit register operations on the unaligned REG_TXPAUSE register (0x522) in rtw_core_enable_beacon(). Specifically, it adds 'rtw_write32_clr(rtwdev, REG_TXPAUSE, BIT_HIGH_QUEUE)' and 'rtw_write32_set(rtwdev, REG_TXPAUSE, BIT_HIGH_QUEUE)', which triggers alignment faults on architectures requiring aligned MMIO accesses.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
wifi: rtw88: handle station mode concurrent scan with AP mode

This patch allows vifs sharing same hardware with the AP
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 96fbb84de4ffce76d54de8656efe0a580081c037
Author: Po-Hao Huang <phhuang@realtek.com>
Date:   Fri Apr 14 20:13:23 2023 +0800

    wifi: rtw88: handle station mode concurrent scan with AP mode
    
    This patch allows vifs sharing same hardware with the AP mode vif to
    do scan, do note that this could lead to packet loss or disconnection
    of the AP's clients. Since we don't have chanctx, update scan info
    upon set channel so bandwidth changes won't go unnoticed and get
    misconf
